topic: Target-clamped FABRIK multi-joint inverse kinematics versus unprojected linearized steps
topic_zh: FABRIK 双向球面投影定长逆运动学与未投影线性步对比
scope: Deterministic 5-bone 3D FABRIK forward-and-backward sphere projection, reachability clamping (R_max = 5.50 u), and vector vs spherical-trig CPU solving. No RigAnything or MagicArticulate neural execution.

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating Node CPU runs after warmup. Direct 3D vector normalization FABRIK pass versus spherical-coordinate trigonometric (acos/atan2/sin/cos) re-parameterization per joint.

protocol.function: clamp ||t - p_0|| <= R_max → backward sphere pass p_N..p_0 → forward sphere pass p_0..p_N → 0 bone stretch

robustness.name: Sampled target angles retain exact bone lengths and zero root slip

good_fit: Multi-joint robotic arms, tentacles, tails, and spines requiring strict bone-length invariance
Out-of-reach target tracking without Jacobian singularity jitter or matrix inversions
Explaining why 3D vector projection beats spherical trigonometry in iterative IK
Real-time procedural animation post-processing over RigAnything / MagicArticulate skeletons
not_for: RigAnything or MagicArticulate autoregressive neural mesh-to-skeleton rigging
Closed-loop parallel Stewart platforms requiring simultaneous multi-branch Jacobian constraints
Full rigid-body torque and actuator-saturation dynamics
2-bone analytical law-of-cosines knees where a single closed-form step suffices
